newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenian shares extend gains, seen stable.
newsitem.headline: Slovenian shares extend gains, seen stable.

text.p: Slovenian shares continued on their upward trek on Tuesday with the blue-chip SBI index rising for the sixth day -- and traders said prices were likely to stay at high levels over the next few days.
"When foreigners return from their holidays, activity will be much more livelier -- over the short term I expect the index to stabilise at these levels," said Tomi Apollonio, an analyst at A Bank.
The SBI index added on 1.46 percent or 23.14 points. Over the last six trading days the index has risen 4.97 percent.
Overall 14 shares rose, six fell and one was flat, while seven were untraded. Turnover climbed to 261.9 million tolars from 171.7 million.
Market participants said the current turnover was mainly thanks to domestic demand.

"Petrol, Krka, Lek and Mercator will remain parade horses of our market also in the future, attracting most foreign interest, but a lot also depends upon what happens on other Eastern European markets," Apollonio said.
Trading firm Kovinotehna was the most actively traded stock, rising 3.06 percent to 572 tolars on volume of 7,082 shares.
Brokerage Dadas was the top gainer, jumping 7.49 percent to 7,890 tolars on volume of 107 shares.
Construction company GPG led decliners, tumbling 4.83 percent to 5,710 tolars on volume of only five shares.
Petrol trader Petrol had the highest turnover, rising 1.95 percent to 26,100 tolars on volume of 3,630 shares for a total of 95.1 million tolars.
Drug company Lek surged 2.66 percent to 37,000 tolars on volume of 1,774 shares for total turnover of 65.4 million tolars.
Market participants said Lek's rise was also helped by information on its good performance in the U.S. where the company exports 10 percent of its total sales.
Lek's strongest competitor Krka, which is listed on the over-the-counter (OTC) section of Ljubljana bourse, firmed 3.49 percent to 27,000 tolars on volume of 2,374 shares.
Trading firm Mercator rose 3.59 percent to 6,060 tolars on volume of 14,152 shares.
Traders said the share was up after its chief executive was reelected on Monday.
